sensory.aromaNotes: Not used as an eating mushroom; industrial fermentations produce citric acid and enzymes, not a savory fruiting-body flavor
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Not a mycoprotein or meat-analog biomass. Relevant because food-grade A. niger enzymes (amylases, pectinases, proteases, glucose oxidase) and citric acid are processing aids in plant- and fungal-protein products. Do not list the mould itself as an ingredient analog.
sensory.preparationContext: Submerged fermentation for acids and enzymes; biomass is generally not the food
sensory.confidenceNotes: Safety reviews support enzyme/acid production strains under current good practice. That is not approval to eat the mycelium as protein.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: No mushroom; black conidial heads on unbranched stipes with vesicles
morphology.sporeCharacteristics: Dark, rough conidia in chains from phialides on a globose vesicle
morphology.microscopyNotes: Same aspergillum body plan as A. oryzae / A. sojae, with black rather than yellow-green heads

nutrition.confidenceNotes: No food-protein proximate is given — listing a protein % would imply the wrong use.

geographic.habitat: Soil, decaying plant matter, indoor environments

strains.availabilityNotes: Classic citric-acid / genome strain — not automatically a food-enzyme production strain.

commercialUse.applicationSummary: Industrial source of citric acid and food enzymes used when processing plant and fungal proteins (hydrolysis, texture, acidity). The organism is a processing microbe, not an analog ingredient. T. reesei in this database is the cellulase counterpart.

productionProcess.title: Submerged fermentation
productionProcess.description: Acid or enzyme recovered from broth; residual biomass is not sold as mycoprotein.

commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Food-use is of purified products, not of the fungus as food.

regulatory.notes: Food-grade enzyme and citric-acid production is longstanding. The mould itself is not an authorized mycoprotein. Some isolates can make ochratoxin or other metabolites — production strains are selected and controlled.

altProteinResearch.title: On the safety of Aspergillus niger — a review
altProteinResearch.summary: Reviews industrial A. niger as an enzyme/acid producer and the controls that keep food-use limited to processed products, not edible biomass.
